text: bicop() expects two approximately uniform columns. fits every requested compatible family selects best according selcrit. Useful family collections include: "", "parametric", "nonparametric"; "oneparametric", "twoparametric", "threeparametric"; "elliptical", "archimedean", "ev", "bbs"; "itau", families compatible Kendall’s tau inversion. title: Rosenblatt and inverse Rosenblatt transforms — rosenblatt
text: Let \((s_1, \ldots, s_d)\) sampling order random vector \(V = (V_1, \ldots, V_d)\) distribution \(F\). continuous variables, Rosenblatt transform \(Z = T(V)\) defined $$   Z_{s_1} = F_{s_1}(V_{s_1}), \qquad   Z_{s_j} = F_{s_j \mid s_1, \ldots, s_{j-1}}   (V_{s_j} \mid V_{s_1}, \ldots, V_{s_{j-1}}),   \quad j = 2, \ldots, d. $$ model correct, components \(Z\) independent standard uniforms. result stored original variable columns; sampling order determines sequence conditional distributions. inverse transform applies corresponding conditional quantiles: $$   V_{s_1} = F_{s_1}^{-1}(Z_{s_1}), \qquad   V_{s_j} = F_{s_j \mid s_1, \ldots, s_{j-1}}^{-1}   (Z_{s_j} \mid V_{s_1}, \ldots, V_{s_{j-1}}),   \quad j = 2, \ldots, d. $$ Thus \(T^{-1}(Z)\) distribution \(F\) \(Z\) contains independent standard uniforms. variable atoms, conditional cdf jumps observation. Let \(G_j\) denote conditional cdf \(V_{s_j}\) given preceding variables sampling order. Following Brockwell (10.1016/j.spl.2007.02.008), rosenblatt() returns $$   Z_{s_j} = W_j G_j(V_{s_j}) + (1 - W_j) G_j(V_{s_j}^{-}), $$ \(G_j(V_{s_j}^{-})\) left limit \(W_j\) independent standard uniforms. randomization used default yields uniform components fitted model. Set randomize_discrete = FALSE return upper endpoint \(G_j(V_{s_j})\) instead.
